subject: kea parrot
title: A Parrot Lands on Sheep at Night and Digs Into Their Backs for Fat

scenes.text: This parrot lands on sheep at night and starts digging.
It's the kea, a mountain parrot from New Zealand's South Island. Sound recorders left in sheep paddocks catch it at work mostly around 2 in the morning.
It drives its hooked beak through the fleece, through the hide, into the back, to reach the high-energy fat around the kidneys.
The sheep can die from the wound itself, from blood poisoning, or from bolting off a ledge in panic. Farmers call it kea strike.
From 1867 to 1970, New Zealand paid a bounty for every kea beak handed in. About 150,000 were killed. Full protection only came in 1986.
Today between 3,000 and 7,000 kea are left. The parrot that hunts sheep is now the one that needs saving.

description:
The kea, New Zealand's mountain parrot, lands on sheep at night and digs through fleece and hide to reach the fat around the kidneys.
Acoustic recorders in strike areas detect kea mostly around 2 am; sheep can die from the wound, from blood poisoning or from injuries while fleeing. Between 1867 and 1970 a bounty was paid for kea beaks and an estimated 150,000 birds were killed; the species was fully protected in 1986 and 3,000 to 7,000 remain.
Would you have guessed a parrot could do this?
